# Temple Scroll Column 66 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 66 | **Condition:** fragmentary toward end

---

**66:1** And the LORD said to me: They have done well in all that they have spoken. A prophet I shall raise up for them from among their brothers, like you,

**66:2** and I shall put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him.

**66:3** And it shall be that the man who does not listen to my words that the prophet shall speak in my name, I myself shall require it of him.

**66:4** But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods — that prophet shall die.

**66:5** And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word that the LORD has not spoken? —

**66:6** when the prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the word does not come to pass and does not come about, that is the word that the LORD has not spoken. In presumption the prophet has spoken it; you shall not fear him.

**66:7** When you come into the land that I am giving to you, and you possess it and dwell in it, and you say: I will set over me a king like all the nations that are around me —

**66:8** you shall surely set over you a king whom I shall choose. From among your brothers you shall set a king over you; you shall not be permitted to set over you a foreign man who is not your brother.

**66:9** Only he shall not multiply horses for himself, and he shall not cause the people to return to Egypt in order to multiply horses, since I have said to you: You shall not return again by this way.

**66:10** And he shall not multiply wives for himself, so that his heart does not turn aside; and silver and gold he shall not multiply for himself exceedingly.

**66:11** And it shall be, when he sits upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself a copy of this instruction upon a scroll, from before the priests, the Levites.

**66:12** And it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, to keep all the words of this instruction and these statutes, to do them,

**66:13** so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers, and so that he does not turn aside from the commandment to the right or to the left, [...] so that he may prolong days upon his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

**66:14** [...] And it shall be, if you surely obey the voice of the LORD your God, to keep and to do all his commandments that I am commanding you this day,

**66:15** [...] the LORD your God shall set you high above all the nations of the earth.

**66:16** And all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, when you obey the voice of the LORD your God. [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 66 completes the prophet-like-Moses law (Deut 18:17–22), presents the law of the king (Deut 17:14–20), and begins the blessings (Deut 28:1–2). The king passage is critical — "whom I shall choose" (first person) replaces Deuteronomy's third person, making God the direct selector of the king. "This instruction" (התורה הזאת) — the Temple Scroll may be referring to ITSELF as the torah the king must copy. Lacunae increase toward end of column. [...] marks genuine manuscript damage.*
